card werk-excerpt-chatlog  [decided]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
Each conversation has its own chat log file beside the decision log, with one JSON line per message
why: The quote must find a conversation's messages from its name alone, and must skip every line that nobody said. One file per conversation, named after the conversation, gives the first. A kind on every line gives the second, so the quote never has to guess what a line is.

To let the quote read one conversation without a search, the chat log of conversation N is the file chats/N.jsonl in the folder that holds the decision log. A conversation name is letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, and does not start with a dot, so a name never points outside that folder.

Each line of the file is one JSON object for one message. It holds the speaker (person or agent), the time the message was written, the session id of the agent session, the kind of the line, and the text. The kind is one of four values: spoken for text that the person typed or the agent wrote, tool_call, tool_result, and tooling for text that the tooling adds. Only a spoken line can hold a quote. A line that is not valid JSON, or has an unknown kind, still counts for the message position, and never holds a quote.

Example:

- Conversation "pricing" has the file chats/pricing.jsonl.
- Line 0 is spoken by the person: "do we bill per seat?"
- Line 1 is a tool_result that prints "seats are the unit we bill".
- Line 2 is spoken by the agent: "seats are the unit we bill".

1. The agent quotes "seats are the unit we bill" from pricing. The quote opens chats/pricing.jsonl.
2. Line 1 holds the words, but its kind is tool_result. It does not count.
3. Line 2 holds the words and is spoken. The excerpt points at message 2.
4. The agent quotes from a conversation "../x". The quote refuses the name and reads no file.

```
.werk/log.jsonl              the decision log
.werk/chats/pricing.jsonl    the chat log of "pricing"
  0  person  spoken       "do we bill per seat?"
  1  agent   tool_result  "seats are the unit we bill"   <- never a match
  2  agent   spoken       "seats are the unit we bill"   <- message 2

0, 1, 2: the message position, counted over every line
```

card werk-chat-log-parts  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
The chat log keeps the open-card line, the person's words, each finished block, and each tool call and its result
why: A later reader of a conversation needs what the agent was told, what it said, and what it did. A streamed token is only an early form of a finished block, so a copy of it would repeat the block. A tool call with its input is the record of an action, and only its own kind keeps it from ever counting as a quote.

To keep the whole conversation readable later, the chat writes one chat log line for each of these, in the order they happen: the open-card line that starts a turn, with the kind tooling; the person's words, spoken by the person; each finished text block of the agent, spoken by the agent; each tool call, with the kind tool_call; each tool result, with the kind tool_result. A tool call line holds the tool name, a space, and the call's input as JSON. A streamed token, a status update and a turn start or end write no line (see #werk-excerpt-chatlog for the kinds).

Example:

- The person sends "Make it three tries" with #retry open.

1. The turn starts. The log gains a tooling line with the open-card line, and a spoken line by the person.
2. The agent streams "Done". Each token goes to the pane only.
3. The agent runs Bash with the command werk show retry. The log gains a tool_call line.
4. The output comes back. The log gains a tool_result line.
5. The block "Done: three tries." finishes. The log gains a spoken line by the agent.

```
 #  speaker  kind         text                                         step
 0  werk     tooling      [the map is now at #retry — ...]             (1)
 1  person   spoken       Make it three tries                          (1)
 -  -        -            D, Do, Don, Done   (tokens: no line)        (2)
 2  agent    tool_call    Bash {"command":"werk show retry"}          (3)
 3  agent    tool_result  card retry [decided] ...                     (4)
 4  agent    spoken       Done: three tries.                           (5)

#  the message position in the chat log.  (n)  the step of the example.
```

card werk-mc-shared-convo-log  [decided]  POSTPONED
Each conversation session is one line in an append-only conversations log beside the map log
why: The server appends one line for each session a tab reports and never rewrites a line, so a session stays listable after its tab moves on to a new one. A store that kept one current session per tab would overwrite the old session.
POSTPONED from #werk-multichat, postponed on 2026-10-24 — 2 hops: werk-mc-shared-convo-log -> werk-mc-fork -> werk-multichat
  Not in werk v0. v0 runs one conversation at a time; tabs, forks and parking wait until v0 is in use. The rules that hold for any single conversation sit under the chat core and stay in v0.
    werk-mc-shared-convo-log -> werk-mc-fork: A fork is its own session with a parent session, as this card decides, so a log line records that parent.
    werk-mc-fork -> werk-multichat: A child card. It refines #werk-multichat.
  This card's link predates the reopen, so re-read it before: werk rederive werk-mc-shared-convo-log

To keep every past session listable, the server appends one line to a conversations log in the same folder as the map log. It appends the line each time a tab's agent reports a session. A line holds the tab name, the session id, the home card when the tab has one (see #werk-mc-split), and the parent session when the tab is a fork (see #werk-mc-fork). No line is ever rewritten. The list of conversations folds the lines into one entry per session id, so a second line for a session the log holds already adds no entry.

**Same area, different decision (no conflict):**
1. `#werk-excerpt-chatlog-fields` (proposed): the five field names of a chat log line. This card decides the file; that card decides the line shape. Its `kind` field repeats the four values listed here.
2. `#werk-chat-log-parts` (proposed): which events write a line. It depends on this card.
3. `#werk-excerpt-pointer` (decided): what an excerpt points at. This card depends on it.

**Overlap to check:**
- `#werk-mc-shared-convo-log` (decided, postponed): one append-only conversations log beside the map log. It records sessions. This card records messages. The two stores do different jobs, but nothing on either card says why there are two.
